name: Eritrea
summary: An Italian colony, then federated with and annexed by Ethiopia; independent in 1993 after a 30-year war; one of the world’s most closed states.

knownFor.label: Asmara modernist city
knownFor.note: Italian modernist buildings, a World Heritage Site.

location.value: The Horn of Africa, bordering the Red Sea; about 117,600 km² (text) or 120,000 km² (infobox).

terrain.value: Cool highlands around Asmara, a hot, dry coastal plain along the Red Sea and the Dahlak Islands.

climate.value: Hot on the coast, mild in the highlands.

resources.value: Gold and silver (Bisha Mine), copper, zinc and Colluli potash.

disasters.value: Droughts and famine have repeatedly hit farmers and herders.

population.value: Sources disagree; Eritrea has never conducted an official government census (infobox: 3.5–6.4 million, 2024).

urbanisation.value: Asmara, the capital, is known for its Italian modernist buildings; Massawa is the main port.

disease.value: Malaria and tuberculosis; health care has improved in rural areas.

migration.value: Large numbers have fled, mostly to Ethiopia, Sudan and Europe, many to escape open-ended national service.

economicBase.value: Subsistence farming and herding, mining (gold, copper, zinc) and money sent by emigrants.

tradeRoutes.value: The Red Sea ports of Massawa and Assab lie on one of the world’s busiest shipping routes.

wealth.value: Not stated as an income group in the article read; HDI 0.503, rated “low” (178th).

moneyAndTax.value: The nakfa, introduced in 1997 after the Ethiopian birr.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A one-party state: the PFDJ is the only legal party.

keyRulers.value: Eritrea has had one president since independence in 1993; he is not named here.

succession.value: National elections have never been held.

institutions.value: The constitution of 1997 was never put into effect, and there is no elected national assembly.

stability.value: Repressive, with indefinite national service and no free press; the country has been in conflict with neighbours, but not in civil war.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: One of the largest armed forces in Africa.

majorWars.value: Eritrean War of Independence (began 1 September 1961; de facto independence 1991). Eritrean–Ethiopian War (1998–2000; about 70,000 deaths).

territoryChange.value: De facto independence 24 May 1991; de jure independence 24 May 1993; admitted to the UN on 28 May 1993.

alliancesRivals.value: A peace treaty with Ethiopia was signed on 9 July 2018.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Primary schooling has expanded, but higher education is limited.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: A railway built by Italy from Massawa to Asmara was rebuilt after independence, mainly for tourist trains.

religion.value: About half are Christian (Orthodox Tewahedo) and half Muslim.

languageWriting.value: Tigrinya, Arabic and English are the three working languages; Eritrea has no official language.

artsArchitecture.value: Art deco architecture in Asmara: more than 400 Italian-designed buildings; UNESCO World Heritage status in 2017.

socialStructure.value: Nine recognised ethnic groups, including the Tigrinya and Tigre.

sharedIdentity.value: The 30-year war of independence (1961–91) is the main source of national identity.

dailyLife.value: Many families eat injera with stew and drink coffee in a traditional ceremony.

ideasReligions.value: Nationalism and self-reliance, shaped by the independence struggle.

colonisation.value: Italian colony from 1890 (proclaimed 1889). The article says Italian rule continued until 1942, followed by British administration until 1950.

riseSignals.value: De facto independence on 24 May 1991; de jure independence on 24 May 1993.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Eritrea continues as an independent state.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
